items.stem: Which one of the following statements about measures of central tendency is correct?
items.answer: The median is not affected by extreme values in the data.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: The mean is strongly affected by extreme values. The mode is the most frequent value; the median is the middle value. It may have more than one mode.
options: The median is not affected by extreme values in the data.
The median is always the most frequent value.
The mean is not affected by extreme values.
A data set can have only one mode.

items.stem: In the study of measures of dispersion, the term 'mean deviation' refers to:
items.answer: The arithmetic average of the absolute deviations of observations from the mean or median
items.markingKey: (b) 'mean deviation' means the arithmetic average of the absolute deviations of observations from the mean or median.
options: The standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, used to compare variability of data sets
The arithmetic average of the absolute deviations of observations from the mean or median
Statistical measures such as mean, median and mode that give a single value representing a data set
The square root of the mean of the squared deviations from the mean

items.stem: The following statement about correlation and rank correlation is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "A correlation coefficient can be greater than +1."

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about correlation and rank correlation is correct?
items.answer: The correlation coefficient lies between −1 and +1.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: In negative correlation one variable increases as the other decreases. It always lies between −1 and +1. Correlation shows association, not necessarily causation.
options: The correlation coefficient lies between −1 and +1.
A high correlation always proves cause and effect.
Negative correlation means both variables increase together.
A correlation coefficient can be greater than +1.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on measures of central tendency and answer the questions that follow.
"For grouped data the mean is calculated by multiplying class marks by frequencies, adding them and dividing by the total frequency. The median is not affected by extreme values in the data. The mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency."
(i) Which measure of central tendency can be found for qualitative data such as the most common soil type? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'mode' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The median is preferred when data contain extreme values. (1)
items.answer: (i) Mode (ii) The value that occurs most frequently in a data set. (iii) It depends only on the middle position and is not affected by very large or very small values.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Mode (ii) The value that occurs most frequently in a data set. (iii) It depends only on the middle position and is not affected by very large or very small values.

items.stem: The following statement about measures of dispersion is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Two data sets with the same mean always have the same spread."
items.answer: Their dispersion can be very different.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Their dispersion can be very different.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about measures of dispersion is correct?
items.answer: Measures of dispersion describe the spread of values around the central value.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: Their dispersion can be very different. That is the range; standard deviation is the root of the mean squared deviation. Range depends only on the highest and lowest values.
options: Measures of dispersion describe the spread of values around the central value.
Range depends on all the values in a data set.
Two data sets with the same mean always have the same spread.
Standard deviation is the difference between the highest and lowest values.
